desk.headline: Revenue up 12% to $1.01bn, above estimates; transaction margin up 32%; full-year outlook reaffirmed
results: Revenue rose 12% to $1.01bn, the fourth quarter in a row above $1bn, and came in ahead of the $964m estimate.
Klarna kept more of each sale: transaction margin dollars jumped 32% to $371m as transaction costs rose only 3%; credit-loss provisions fell to 0.56% of volume from 0.72%.
Volume grew 10% to $36.1bn, led by the US (+24%) and Fair Financing, its longer-term loans, up 61% to $5.2bn.
Adjusted operating income was $21m (a $35m swing), but higher share-based pay left a net loss of $65m, or $0.19 a share, smaller than last year's $95m loss.
Klarna Card volume more than doubled to $4.5bn and subscription revenue rose over 500% to $43m; about $7.7bn of loans were sold to outside buyers.

guidance.summary: Klarna repeated its full-year 2026 outlook, which implies Q4 revenue of $1.02–1.10bn and adjusted operating income of $100–120m. It expects a positive net income in Q4.

points: Management said Q4 has started well: revenue, transaction margin and adjusted operating income are tracking above the outlook, with US volume growing close to 30% so far.
Klarna is aiming for record Q4 numbers and positive net income, helped by payment-processor partners such as Fiserv's Clover going live before the holidays.
Expanding Fair Financing in Europe, where only about 10% of users have tried it versus 35% in the US, is a main goal for 2027.
A slight rise in Fair Financing late payments was blamed on adding the Klarna Card to that book; Pay Later delinquencies improved.
No 2027 guidance yet; slower UK growth, a currency headwind and customs changes for drop-shipped goods were named as drags.
